name: SeismicShield-RL
description: SeismicShield-RL is a preregistered simulation study evaluating multi-agent reinforcement learning for friction-damper retrofit co-design under earthquake uncertainty. The primary objective is to determine whether a story-decomposed MAPPO/CTDE approach can improve the cost–drift–acceleration Pareto trade-off relative to transparent heuristics, evolutionary optimization, NSGA-II, single-agent PPO, and decentralized IPPO under controlled and equal computational budgets. The final preregistration design uses 34 earthquake events from the European Strong-Motion Database (ESM), with four explicitly licensed horizontal acceleration records per event, for a total of 136 records. Only source-reported CC-BY3_0-IT and CC-BY4_0 waveforms are eligible; records with unknown or network-default licensing are excluded without reinterpretation. The frozen event split is 13 training events, 5 validation events, 4 pilot events permanently excluded from confirmatory inference, and 12 confirmatory events. The study combines a calibrated fast nonlinear MDOF simulator for high-throughput learning with OpenSeesPy as the high-fidelity reference simulator for primary confirmatory claims. Structural families include 3-, 6-, 10-, and 20-story buildings. Primary outcomes include normalized Pareto hypervolume, maximum inter-story drift ratio, peak floor acceleration, out-of-distribution degradation, and risk-sensitive performance.
